  "importance_rationale": "The sign problem is the central practical obstruction to quantum Monte Carlo across condensed matter, chemistry, and nuclear physics, and the source paper (Hangleiter, Roth, Nagaj, Eisert, Science Advances 2020) both delivers a working easing methodology and proves easing NP-complete only 'in general ... for nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians and simple basis choices'. Classifying which structured, physically motivated families fall on the tractable side of that boundary would directly determine where measure-driven basis-change easing can be deployed and where it provably cannot, guiding method development and simulation strategy. Importance is medium rather than high because the question is an open-ended classification across families: any single result settles one family, the generic worst-case barrier is already known, and the question is a derived open boundary of one paper's framework rather than a named, field-defining problem. The candidate is not a famous or named problem, so no authoritative-formulation alignment check applies; the statement faithfully tracks the source's 'in general' qualifier without imposing any family, geometry, or basis restriction beyond the source framing. This gates the later-literature audit, which should check whether follow-up work to arXiv:1906.02309 has already classified easing complexity for specific families.",
  "scientific_significance_score": 7,
  "scientific_significance_rationale": "A positive result (a polynomial-time easing algorithm for a physically motivated Hamiltonian family) would change capability: it would certify that measure-based basis optimization is a scalable, principled preprocessing step for QMC on that family rather than a heuristic, enlarging the set of simulable models. A negative result (family-specific hardness or impossibility) would change knowledge with a sharp bound: it would show the NP-completeness barrier already bites inside physically relevant structure, redirecting effort away from basis-search approaches for those families toward stoquasticity-avoiding formulations or other algorithms. Either outcome sharpens the complexity map between stoquastic (efficiently simulable) and generic Hamiltonians, complementing known complexity results about the sign problem itself with a classification of the meta-task of easing it.",
  "expected_result": "A submission specifies a physically motivated family of quantum many-body Hamiltonians (stated explicitly, with its structure and physical motivation) and settles the easing task for it in the source's measure-based sense. A positive submission contains: (i) an explicit classical algorithm that outputs efficiently computable basis changes for arbitrary instances of the family, (ii) a proof that its runtime is polynomial in instance size, and (iii) a rigorous argument, supported where appropriate by numerical demonstration on representative family instances, that the produced basis changes reduce an efficiently computable measure of non-stoquasticity as defined in the source framework. A negative submission contains a proof that no such polynomial-time easing algorithm exists for the stated family (under standard complexity assumptions), via reduction or impossibility argument specific to that family rather than a restatement of the known generic NP-completeness. The answer format committed to by the source question is preserved: a classification of families into those admitting polynomial-time easing and those not, delivered family by family.",

  "verification_standard": "A submission must (a) explicitly define the Hamiltonian family it addresses and argue that the family is physically motivated and not artificially constructed to trivialize easing, and (b) make one of two claims. Positive branch: submit the easing algorithm together with a proof of polynomial runtime in instance size and evidence that the output basis changes reduce an efficiently computable non-stoquasticity measure for the family — a proof of the reduction for the family, plus numerical measurements of the measure before and after the basis change on a stated set of representative instances, with model, basis, and measure conventions pinned. Negative branch: submit a family-specific hardness or impossibility proof whose statement is about the stated family and whose argument does not merely re-derive the known generic NP-completeness for nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians and simple basis choices. It passes if the claimed tractability or hardness is rigorous for the stated family, 'easing' and the non-stoquasticity measure match the source framework (no redefinition of easing, no restriction of basis changes or instances beyond the source's framing), and the result is not subsumed by the already-published generic result. Each per-family result is checked on its own; the parent question is naturally answered by an accumulating classification, so a verified per-family claim is a faithful answer unit, not a restricted substitute.",

  "verification_difficulty_rationale": "The result genuinely answers the source question if it settles easing complexity for a stated physically motivated family under the source's measure-based definition of easing; what remains open after any single submission is the rest of the classification, which is inherent to a 'for which families' question rather than a defect. Cheapest sound branch governs the score. Positive branch: the numerical part — running the submitted algorithm on pinned family instances and measuring the non-stoquasticity measure before and after — is a replayable procedure (R) and is delegable, but the load-bearing claims are the proof that runtime is polynomial and the proof that easing holds for the whole family (an asymptotic/uniform claim that finite instances cannot discharge), so the residual is derivation review of connected proofs using standard algorithmic and Hamiltonian-algebra technique: score in the 4-6 band. Negative branch: a family-specific MAXCUT-style hardness reduction is pure derivation review of moderate depth with standard reduction machinery, likewise 4-6. Specification fidelity adds a modest residual: the reviewer must confirm the stated family is a genuine physically motivated class and that the measure and easing notion match the source paper rather than a weakened redefinition — a local check, not a substantial reconstruction. No long, fragile, or novel chain is required by the contract, and no witness-only certificate settles either branch, so the residual sits at 5: connected but standard derivations, with the replayable numeric component delegable and not lowering the structural burden below the derivation floor.",
